title: Negative Sentiment Continues To Drive Market Direction
text:
Shutterstock photo Monday, November 19, 2018, 12:26 PM, EST
NASDAQ Composite -2.42% Dow -1.43% S&P 500 -1.41% Russell 2000 -1.22% NASDAQ Advancers: 777 Decliners: 1433 Today's Volume (vs Friday) -9.25% Crude $68.05 -$0.34 , Gold $1337.40 -$0.25, VIX 20.28 +2.14 Market Movers
Tech Sector & Consumer Discretionary continues to give markets pause Apple (AAPL) announced production cuts, trades near 4 month low Facebook (FB) makes new 52 week low Energy pulling back as Oil continues to underperform Failure of final joint statement at APEC summit refreshes US-China trade tensions NAHB November Housing Market Index sentiment decreases to 60 vs 67 consensus Chris's Commentary
U.S. equity markets opened in negative territory and continue to trade lower. Trading volumes on the consolidated tape are the lowest in a week since Veterans Day when the bond markets were closed. Negative sentiment continues to drive market direction.
As mega-cap tech leaders continue to trend lower following production cuts, negative PR and renewed China-U.S. trade concerns. Currently 9 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are trading lower with Tech and Consumer Discretionary sectors the worst performing.
Financials are the best performing sector following dovish FED speak over the weekend. Crude is negative on the day, but rallying back from the morning lows. Gold and the dollar both are trading lower as well. The yield on the 10-yr continues to retreat and now stands at 3.061%.
Josh Elman from Nasdaq's Corporate Solutions Consumer Team stated, "Despite lofty expectations heading into the holiday season, the retail space has been selling-off recently, as investors look to take profits toward the end of 2018. The sector will be in focus this week as a number of retail bellwethers report 3Q18 results, and investors seek commentary on the upcoming holiday season.
Given last week's reaction to 3Q18 earnings, the risk is likely to the downside, especially with the holiday-shortened week and recent broader market bearishness."
Thanksgiving week is traditionally one of the strongest weeks for the U.S. equity market. Briefing.com stated, "Bearing a holiday-shortened schedule and a close on the busiest shopping day for the year at a seasonal time that is often the start of the year-end scramble for exposure from the left-behind's of the fund management world as they sweat over benchmarks and bonuses…"
However, this year may be different as concerns about Brexit, tariffs, oil and Tech continue to grab headlines. With negative sentiment still the dominant trading-trend, will the markets rally this week to give us a Happy Thanksgiving?

Brian's Technical Take
Is the short end of the curve topping?
There is a lot of interpretation making the rounds regarding last week's Fed-speak by Chairman Powell and other policy makers inside the Federal Reserve. Some argue nothing was said that has not already been spoken before, while others believe an intentional, less hawkish message was delivered in order to sooth volatile markets. Whatever the cause both the US dollar and treasury yields saw a "dovish" move lower from 52-week highs.
While a December rate hike is widely expected (70% + probability), the consensus for three additional rate hikes in 2019 is debatable. One market measure some look to as a barometer of future rate hikes is the 2-year Treasury Yield which peaked earlier this month at 2.97%, its highest since June 2008.
As the yield was making fresh highs, a bearish divergence had been forming over the last two months with the daily RSI already making a series of lower highs since peaking in late September. The 2-year yield has now been flat or in the red for seven consecutive sessions and its daily RSI is making a six month low.
Today it is breaching the 2.79% level which has been a clearly defined support line since early October.
If seasonal risk on forces can kick in soon, one could see the 2-year rally towards last week's "gap" at the 2.90% - 2.92% level. This actually would be concerning as many technicians will then likely highlight the potential "head & shoulder" topping pattern which could be significant given the 178 bps rally realized over the prior 14 months.
It remains to be seen whether the recent weakness is attributable to common short term positioning, Fed-speak, or something more meaningful such as expectations on future economic activity. We will keep you updated as this price action unfolds throughout the remainder of 2018.
